commands.name: reminder_create
commands.description: Adds a reminder to a list, or the default list.

args.name: title
args.meaning: One non-empty line.

args.name: list
args.meaning: The list to add it to; the default list if not given.

args.name: due
args.meaning: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" in local time or "YYYY-MM-DD"; needs background mode, and 00:00 is refused.

args.name: notes
args.meaning: The reminder's notes.

args.name: priority
args.meaning: "high", "medium" or "low"; needs background mode.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: "ui" or "background"; use one of this command's modes.

example_requests: Remind me to call the dentist
Add milk to my Shopping list
Add a reminder to pay rent on 1 December at 9am
commands.precondition: Reminders' local account is available, and the program has Automation permission for Reminders. For ui mode, the program also has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: One new reminder exists with these values.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the change wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: the screen holds typed text or another app came to the front; nothing is changed

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: no reminder has that title, or no list has that name; nothing is changed

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: the mode can't do this, including due or priority in ui mode

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
Only the local account was tested, with no iCloud or other account signed in to Reminders.
Due dates and priority can't be set in ui mode because the date field exposes no parts to Accessibility, so use background mode.
A due time of 00:00 is refused because it can't be told apart from a day without a time.
UI mode depends on English names and was tested only in English.

commands.name: reminder_list
commands.description: Lists reminders in a list or in every list, newest first.

args.name: list
args.meaning: Only look in the list with this name.

args.name: completed
args.meaning: False for open ones, True for done ones, None for both.

args.name: limit
args.meaning: The most reminders to return.

args.name: fields
args.meaning: Fields to return, as a comma-separated string or a list; adds id and completed_date if asked.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "background": this command has no verified ui mode.

example_requests: What's on my Shopping list?
Show my reminders
What have I completed in Work?
